sources.entry: Request Inbox - Collect and inspect HTTP requests for testing and debugging. Create and manage inboxes, capture detailed request data, configure custom responses. (Demo, Source Code) Apache-2.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Request Inbox is a self-hostable web app for collecting and inspecting incoming HTTP requests, a free alternative to webhook.site and webhookinbox.com.
summary.what_it_does: It lets you create, list, and delete inboxes that capture incoming HTTP requests with headers, body, and metadata, and view them in a web UI with a JSON viewer and auto-refresh. Each inbox can be configured with custom response headers and body, optionally as a Go template when marked dynamic. Callbacks forward a captured request to another service with forwarded headers and a templated body, and a callback can be retried. Inboxes can be private, and access is handled through GitHub or Google OAuth or API keys. The backend is a Go API with an MCP server and an OpenAPI 3.1 spec, and the frontend is React with a browser WebMCP tool layer.
use_cases: Debug HTTP requests from third-party services
Test outgoing callbacks and their responses
Serve custom mock HTTP responses for testing
Give AI agents access to inboxes via MCP
how_to_run: cd api && make install && make run-api-hot
notable: Single Docker container bundling nginx and the Go API, with images on Docker Hub and GitHub Container Registry
Backend MCP server with tools for creating inboxes, listing and clearing captured requests, and managing callbacks
Browser WebMCP tools and forms that let agents act in the active session
Strict callback URL policy in production that blocks private, loopback, and link-local destinations and pins DNS-checked IPs
Can also run as an AWS Lambda behind API Gateway
caveats: Production callback destinations are restricted; the local development and Compose policy is permissive and must not be used as-is in production
Planned features such as alerts, import/export, request pass/fail testing, and limits are not yet implemented
Production deployment described targets AWS infrastructure via Terraform and GitHub Actions
